Dear Colleague,

Thank you for accepting the referral of Ms. Thompson, whom I have followed for five years for well-controlled hypertension.

She reports exertional chest tightness over the past six weeks, relieved by rest, most often when walking uphill. A resting electrocardiogram on 2026-09-18 showed normal sinus rhythm with no acute changes. Her current medications are lisinopril 10 mg daily and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly.

Requested consultation: Cardiology, first visit.
Reason for referral: exertional chest pain, risk stratification.

Interpretation assistance is not required; the patient is fluent in English and asks that correspondence be sent to the telephone number above.

Sincerely,
Dr. Harold Nkemdirim, MD

LAKESHORE DIAGNOSTICS - CARDIAC IMAGING
Report issued: 2026-09-29

Patient: Avery Thompson
Date of birth: 1984-03-12
Referring physician: Dr. Harold Nkemdirim, MD
Study: Transthoracic echocardiogram with colour Doppler

Findings:
Left ventricular ejection fraction is estimated at 58 percent. Left ventricular chamber size is normal. There is mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Diastolic function is grade I (impaired relaxation). The left atrium is mildly dilated at 4.2 cm. No valvular stenosis. Trace mitral regurgitation. The right ventricle is normal in size and function. No pericardial effusion.

Interpretation:
Preserved systolic function with grade I diastolic dysfunction and mild concentric hypertrophy, consistent with long-standing hypertension. No structural cause for exertional symptoms was identified on this study.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. If symptoms persist, exercise stress testing may be considered.

Electronically signed by Dr. Susan Whitfield, MD, Cardiology

Report issued: 2026-10-09
Patient: Daniel Okafor
Date of birth: 1979-11-02
Study: Transthoracic echocardiogram with colour Doppler

Findings:
Left ventricular ejection fraction is estimated at 62 percent. Normal chamber sizes. Normal wall thickness. Grade I diastolic function. The left atrium is normal at 3.6 cm. No valvular stenosis or significant regurgitation. No thrombus. No pericardial effusion. The right heart is normal.

Rhythm strip recorded during the study showed frequent premature atrial contractions, occurring in short runs of three to five beats.

Interpretation:
Normal left ventricular systolic function. Frequent premature atrial contractions, which correlate with the patient's reported palpitations. Recommend clinical correlation and consideration of ambulatory rhythm monitoring.

Electronically signed by Dr. Priya Nadkarni, MD, Cardiology

LAKEVIEW REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - NEUROLOGY
Outpatient clinic note

Date of issue: 2026-09-15
Patient: Jonah Feldman
Date of birth: 1968-05-17
Seen by: Dr. Jonas Petersen, MD, Movement Disorders

History:
Mr. Feldman has a four-year history of a right-sided resting tremor with progressive slowness of gait. He has been managed with carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily with a partial response. Over the past six months he reports increasing difficulty with balance and two falls without injury.

Examination:
Alert and orientated. Resting tremor of the right hand, mild cogwheel rigidity bilaterally, bradykinesia on finger tapping. Postural reflexes are impaired. No pyramidal signs. Cranial nerves intact.

Assessment:
Idiopathic Parkinson disease, Hoehn and Yahr stage 2, with recent postural instability.

Plan:
Continue current medication. Referral discussed for consideration of advanced therapy. The patient has asked for a consultation that specifically addresses deep brain stimulation candidacy, which is outside this clinic's scope and is not provided at this centre.
